Account 4521 is the subject of this Suspicious Activity Report. Between September 11, 2022, at 13:11 and September 16, 2022, at 07:08, the account received 27 inbound ACH transactions from nine distinct counterparty accounts, collectively identified through graph analysis as a fan-in ring network. Total inbound funds during this seven-day period amounted to $254,317.25. Of that amount, $216,169.66, representing 85 percent of inbound funds, was moved back out of the account within 48 hours, consistent with rapid movement typology indicative of layering activity.

The transaction pattern demonstrates strong structuring indicators. Eleven of the inbound deposits fell between $9,500 and $10,000 and occurred between September 11 and September 16, 2022, with 100 percent of those funds subsequently consolidated and moved back out within seven days. A broader pattern of 27 transactions ranging from $9,083.75 to $9,902.70 was also identified within the same window, all deliberately maintained below the $10,000 Currency Transaction Report threshold.

The combined typologies of fan-in aggregation, structured deposits, and near-immediate outbound consolidation are consistent with coordinated efforts to evade reporting requirements and obscure the origin of funds. The nine contributing counterparties, identified as RING-M01 through RING-M06 among others in partial transaction records, transmitted funds at irregular hours, including overnight and early morning, further supporting a coordinated scheme. Based on the totality of evidence, this institution recommends filing a Suspicious Activity Report with FinCEN and escalating to the Financial Intelligence Unit for further investigation and potential account restriction.

typologies.name: STRUCTURING_HIGH
typologies.what: Deliberately breaking a large sum into deposits that each stay under the $10,000 reporting threshold, then moving the pooled money on.
typologies.rule: 5+ deposits between $9,500 and $10,000 into one account within 7 days, AND at least 60% of it sent back out within 7 days.
typologies.why: The onward transfer is what separates laundering from an ordinary cash business: a shop banks its takings and leaves them; a mule account gathers and forwards.

typologies.name: STRUCTURING_MEDIUM
typologies.what: The same sub-threshold deposit pattern, but without a confirmed onward transfer.
typologies.rule: 3+ transactions between $9,000 and $10,000 within 7 days, either side of the account.
typologies.why: A weaker indicator on its own, since plenty of legitimate businesses look like this, so it can put an account in front of an analyst but never escalates it by itself.

typologies.name: RAPID_MOVEMENT
typologies.what: Money arriving from several sources and leaving again almost immediately: a pass-through or funnel account.
typologies.rule: 80%+ of inbound funds sent out within 48 hours, on at least $1,000 gathered from 2+ distinct senders.
typologies.why: Requiring more than one sender is what distinguishes a funnel from ordinary two-party settlement, where fast in-and-out is normal.

typologies.name: VELOCITY
typologies.what: A sudden burst of activity far outside what this account normally does.
typologies.rule: Peak transactions-per-hour more than 4 standard deviations above the account's own baseline, once it has 10+ prior transactions.
typologies.why: The history minimum matters: a standard deviation from three transactions is noise, not a baseline.

typologies.name: HIGH_RISK_AMOUNT
typologies.what: A single transaction wildly out of character for the account.
typologies.rule: One amount more than 4 standard deviations above the account's own history, with 10+ prior transactions.
typologies.why: Same reasoning as velocity: the account is compared against itself, not the population.

typologies.name: FAN_IN_RING
typologies.what: Many accounts feeding one collector account, which then forwards the pooled money on: the classic smurfing ring.
typologies.rule: 5+ distinct senders into one account within 7 days, with 60%+ of the gathered total moving onward.
typologies.why: Found on the transaction graph rather than in any single account's numbers, which is why it corroborates the rules rather than repeating them.

typologies.name: CYCLE
typologies.what: Money that travels through several accounts and returns near where it started: layering to obscure its origin.
typologies.rule: A closed loop of 3 to 5 hops on the transfer graph.
typologies.why: Two-party back-and-forth is excluded deliberately, since that's just two people who both pay each other, which is extremely common and not laundering.

submit.conversational_text:
Structuring, often called smurfing, is an anti-money-laundering term for breaking down a large sum of money into multiple smaller transactions. Individuals do this to intentionally keep each transfer below regulatory reporting thresholds or bank monitoring limits to avoid automatic flagging.
